from: A guesthouse owner spends every Friday personally doing the bookkeeping, which would cost N$2 600 a month to outsource. The same time spent visiting corporate clients has brought in bookings worth an estimated N$11 000 a month whenever she has done it. State what the opportunity cost of the bookkeeping arrangement is and what it means for her.
to: A guesthouse owner spends every Friday doing the bookkeeping herself, which would cost N$2 600 a month to outsource. Using the same Fridays to visit corporate clients has brought in bookings worth an estimated N$11 000 a month whenever she has done it. Explain what the opportunity cost of doing the bookkeeping herself means for her.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks (one point, applied to the context), keeping the opportunity-cost comparison it teaches.

from: A start-up's cash-flow forecast shows the cumulative bank balance falling to minus N$126 000 in month five and returning to positive in month nine. State what this tells the founder and what it tells a provider of finance.
to: A start-up's cash-flow forecast shows the cumulative bank balance falling to minus N$126 000 in month five and returning to positive in month nine. Explain what these figures mean for the founder.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks and narrowed to the founder, so the card asks for one point applied to the forecast.

from: Identify the four factors of production and state what each one contributes to output.
to: Identify the four factors of production and what each one contributes to output.
why: State is not used on the current AS papers; that part now instructs with Identify, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Classify each of these and explain your reasoning: a butchery serving one suburb of Windhoek; a supermarket chain with branches in Windhoek, Walvis Bay, Oshakati and Katima Mulilo; a Namibian beef processor shipping to the European Union from one abattoir at Okahandja; and that same processor after it buys an abattoir in Botswana.
to: Identify whether each of these is a local, national, international or multinational business, and explain your reasoning: a butchery serving one suburb of Windhoek; a supermarket chain with branches in Windhoek, Walvis Bay, Oshakati and Katima Mulilo; a Namibian beef processor shipping to the European Union from one abattoir at Okahandja; and that same processor after it buys an abattoir in Botswana.
why: Classify is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify and Explain, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Set out the stages an entrepreneur goes through in turning an idea into a trading business, and say what each stage produces.

why: Set out is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify, in order. It asks for the whole sequence, which the papers ask for one point at a time, so it is kept as a recall card with no paper tariff.

from: A development agency is reviewing why so many of the businesses it funded three years ago have closed. Set out the questions it should ask about each closed business, and say what the answer to each would tell it.
to: A development agency is reviewing why so many of the businesses it funded three years ago have closed. Identify the questions it should ask about each closed business, and explain what the answer to each would tell it.

from: Hilma has N$60 000 of savings and a signed order from one guest lodge for laundry services worth N$18 000 a month. A machine large enough for the lodge costs N$95 000; she has been offered N$40 000 of external finance secured against her vehicle, leaving a gap. The lodge's contract runs for twelve months and it takes 70% of her forecast revenue. Analyse the barriers she faces and the risks she is taking on, and recommend whether she should proceed.
to: Hilma has N$60 000 of savings and a signed order from one guest lodge for laundry services worth N$18 000 a month. A machine large enough for the lodge costs N$95 000; she has been offered N$40 000 of external finance secured against her vehicle, leaving a gap. The lodge's contract runs for twelve months and it takes 70% of her forecast revenue. Analyse the barriers she faces and the risks she is taking on, and evaluate whether she should proceed.
why: Recommend is not used on the current AS papers; the judgement is now asked for with Evaluate. The card keeps its Analyse part, so it pairs the two parts of a Paper 1 Section B question (8 + 12) and no single paper tariff is claimed.
